answers.answer: dotnet/runtime supplies .NET execution engines, class libraries, and shared-host/installers for supported platforms. Managed applications call its libraries and run on its runtimes. Users start applications via dotnet or apphost; native programs can load .NET through nethost, and COM activation uses comhost. Hosting resolves frameworks via hostfxr, then hostpolicy loads/configures CoreCLR and starts the application. These are architectural entry points, not an exhaustive inventory of external callers.

Principal components: CoreCLR (execution engine used by most workloads), Mono (mobile, browser WebAssembly and WASI execution), System.Private.CoreLib (lowest managed layer coupled to the runtime), libraries (other assemblies, sources and tests), and hosts/installers/packs (startup, hosting libraries, framework distributions). Beyond HTTP, runtime responsibilities include garbage collection, type/memory safety, interoperation and debugging/profiling; libraries provide primitives, collections and operating-system services such as files. Native library shims connect managed libraries to OS dependencies.

The execution engines are C/C++; the inspected HTTP implementation/tests are C#. Root build.sh/build.cmd orchestrate component subsets, configurations and target OS/architecture. Managed projects use Microsoft.NET.Sdk/MSBuild and dotnet build; native library builds use CMake with clang. Boundaries include managed libraries versus native OS shims, runtime-specific CoreLib versus runtime-agnostic library code, and build platform versus target platform. HTTP has explicit compile-time platform branches: browser/WASI handlers differ from sockets; mobile selects separate HttpClientHandler sources. This is a verified principal-language/build outline, not an exhaustive language census or compiler-support audit.

Selecting HttpClient.GetAsync on the desktop sockets-backed handler: its overloads create a GET HttpRequestMessage and enter HttpClient.SendAsync; that calls base.SendAsync (HttpMessageInvoker), which dispatches to its configured handler. Default HttpClient constructs HttpClientHandler, whose non-browser/non-WASI implementation wraps SocketsHttpHandler and forwards SendAsync. SocketsHttpHandler validates the request, lazily schedules SetupHandlerChain when needed, then sends through the resulting stage. Alternatively new HttpClient(new SocketsHttpHandler()) bypasses HttpClientHandler. Arbitrary user-supplied handlers and mobile/native builds are separate boundaries.

X is RedirectHandler.SendAsync, gated by private RequestRequiresForceGet. For 300/301/302 only POST becomes GET; 303 rewrites methods other than GET/HEAD; 307/308 retain methods. Rewriting also clears Content and disables chunked transfer.

SetupHandlerChain clones/normalizes HttpConnectionSettings; constructs HttpConnectionPoolManager and HttpConnectionHandler (credential-dependent request auth); conditionally wraps MetricsHandler and creates SocketsHttpHandlerMetrics, then DiagnosticsHandler, then RedirectHandler, then invokes the decompression factory. The factory constructs DecompressionHandler. Thus enabled send order is decompression → redirect → diagnostics → metrics → connection handler. It directly consults GlobalHttpSettings, DistributedContextPropagator, CredentialCache and supported decompression flags, then atomically publishes _handler with Interlocked.CompareExchange and disposes a losing chain. Optional stages depend on settings.

For an allowed sockets POST→302: PostAsync creates the POST/content and enters the q4 dispatch path. RedirectHandler sends inward through optional telemetry stages → HttpConnectionHandler → pool manager → selected pool. Protocol/authentication/proxy selection is dynamic; HTTP/1.x reaches HttpConnection.SendAsync. On the 302, RedirectHandler disposes the old response, clears Authorization, updates RequestUri, changes POST to GET, clears Content/chunking, conditionally disables authentication, and resends inward. It returns the eventual response, not necessarily 200. Missing/blocked Location or an exceeded redirect limit instead stops following.

The evidenced direct construction consumer is SocketsHttpHandler.SetupHandlerChain: when automatic redirects are enabled it passes the maximum, current inner chain, and disableAuthOnRedirect = credentials is not CredentialCache. Constructor-contract changes directly affect this site; semantic changes affect its redirect-enabled requests. No exhaustive consumer search was completed.

HttpClientHandlerTest_AutoRedirect.AllowAutoRedirect_True_ValidateNewMethodUsedOnRedirection uses RedirectStatusCodesOldMethodsNewMethods: 300/301/302/303/307/308 crossed with GET, HEAD, POST, DELETE, OPTIONS, PATCH, PUT and a custom method. Two loopback servers verify the redirected method and final 200. AllowAutoRedirect_True_PostToGetDoesNotSendTE covers 300–303 and asserts GET without Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length. SocketsHttpHandlerTest_AutoRedirect inherits these tests and excludes browser/WASI. The test project includes the shared test source; factories create HttpClientHandler and HttpClient(handler), entering the public send pipeline described in q4. Tests call client.SendAsync(TestAsync, request); that helper's body was not located, so its exact sync/async adapter edge remains unverified. These tests were inspected, not executed.

On the inspected HTTP/1 path, received header bytes enter HttpConnection.AddResponseHeader: whitespace is trimmed, the descriptor/value decoded, and response.Headers receives TryAddWithoutValidation. KnownHeaders.Location selects UriHeaderParser.RelativeOrAbsoluteUriParser; HttpResponseHeaders.Location calls GetSingleParsedValue, which parses raw stored values. UriHeaderParser uses Uri.TryCreate, with a UTF-8 decoding fallback. RedirectHandler.GetUriForRedirect accepts redirect statuses, reads Location, resolves relative URIs against RequestUri, inherits an absent fragment, and rejects insecure downgrades/unsupported schemes. SendAsync assigns the result to request.RequestUri before resending. HTTP/2/3 wire-header entry points were not traced.

limitations: Static, pinned-source inspection only; no builds or test executions. No local source checkout, Lattice, MCP, oracle, prior-answer access, or delegation.

Citation ranges use the web tool's numbered raw-source rendering (or explicitly web-rendered GitHub page), not asserted physical GitHub file line numbers. The browser normalizes blank lines: RedirectHandler's raw rendering has 170 lines while its GitHub page reports 189 source lines. Symbols are included to disambiguate.
Transport choice, optional stages, credentials, proxies, custom handlers and server responses are dynamic boundaries. No exhaustive whole-repository caller or language census was performed.
The TestAsync extension/helper implementation was not located; its call sites and factories were verified.
Authoritative token telemetry is unavailable and is not estimated.
Exact delivery/start timestamp was not recorded. selfReportedStartedAt is the first clock observation after research had begun; it is not used to claim measured elapsed duration.
